_doc: Which frontend pages the capture gate scores against retail, and what each
scored when it was last measured. Consumed by
tools/score_frontend_capture.py, which Capture-Frontend.ps1 calls.
`measured` is the FACT. The gate's ceiling is DERIVED from it as
min(measured + marginPp, 100) at load time and is deliberately NOT stored
here - it was, briefly, as 30 values that were each exactly measured + 2.0,
and two copies of one fact drift. Use `regressionCeilingOverride` on a page
if some region ever needs a bound other than the blanket margin, with a
comment saying why. None does today.
A ceiling is NOT a parity claim - title-logo is 29.48% wrong. The canonical
explanation of that distinction is the module docstring of
tools/score_frontend_capture.py; do not restate it, point at it.
Ceilings apply to the WORST sample, never the mean - a regression visible at
one video phase is still a regression.
A STALE `measured` IS A DEAD GATE, AND THAT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. From
8618e773 (2026-07-27) to 2026-07-28 this file held FEP_MAIN@entry FULL FRAME
= 71.47 while the build measured 7.53 - a ceiling of 73.47 guarding a value
of 7.53, nine times loose. It could not have failed for any regression short
of the page not drawing at all. 8618e773 said so in its own message
('Ceilings are NOT re-derived here') and nothing in npm test notices, so the
re-derivation is a DELIBERATE ACT that has to be scheduled by a human. Do it
in the same session as any change that moves these numbers.

_measurementProvenance.staleReason: The released language row, cursor, decor shadow, and frontend composition changed after the measured build. Preserve these measurements as history; remeasure from a fresh clean production main-menu capture before gating again.
_measuredAtCommitNote: Re-derived with tools/score_frontend_capture.py --measure from a capture
The main working tree was DIRTY with unrelated in-flight work at the time,
which would have forced the purpose stamp down to 'probe'. Rather than
measure the dirt or disturb it, the capture was taken from a detached
`git worktree` at HEAD, which is clean by construction. That is why this
block can name a commit and mean it.
WHAT THIS REPLACED. The previous values were measured at 0c96fb1d on
2026-07-27 and were correct for that build - re-measuring
mainmenu-clean-0c96fb1d today still reproduces all 30 of them exactly. They
went stale when 8618e773 landed the staged main-menu reveal and explicitly
did not re-derive. Seventeen of the thirty numbers had drifted; the worst
was FEP_MAIN@entry lang-selector at 99.72 stored against 0.00 measured.
@settled did not move on any of its ten regions.
captureDeterminism: Two full mainmenu captures of 684c7c52 taken back to back were
byte-identical on all 161 frames, and the pair taken at 432c53f7 on
2026-07-28 reproduces every one of these thirty numbers. Our own
contribution to run-to-run variance is 0.00%, so the 2.00pp margin is
entirely headroom against incidental change, not an allowance for flake.
THE MARGIN DOES NOT NEED TO COVER RETAIL'S CROSS-RUN FLOOR, and must not be
widened on the argument that it should. That floor reaches 8.95% on
lang-selector @settled and 7.15% on bg-empty-left @settled, both far above
2.00pp - but the gated statistic is gapPct, which discards floor-unstable
pixels ONE AT A TIME before counting. The floor is already gone from the
number the ceiling bounds. What the margin covers is our own variance,

_windowNote: FEP_MAIN is gated as THREE windows rather than one, because retail builds
the page up in stages and a single window would hide a regression behind
the stage we are worst at.
Measured 2026-07-27 from the retail run1 burst, region mean RGB:
t000014  lang-selector, menu-column and the arcs are ALL exactly the
flat fill (23,23,48). Only title-logo and bg-emblem-topright
are drawn. Retail's first main-menu frame carries background
plus logo plus emblem and NOTHING ELSE.
t000524  all chrome present and over-bright (lang-selector 66,82,122)
t001020+ settling to its steady value (lang-selector 58,52,74)
SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28, and left here because the reasoning is why the three
windows exist. This read: 'We draw the entire page on frame 0, which is why
the entry window scores 76% gap against a retail cross-run floor of 0.24% -
retail is perfectly reproducible there and we simply differ. That is a real
defect, tracked separately.' It WAS, and 8618e773 closed it by porting
retail's 50-frame staged reveal: the entry window is now 7.53% against the
same 0.24% floor, and seven of its nine named regions are at or under 0.30%.
The three windows earned their keep exactly as intended. A single window
would have averaged a 76% defect into a ~20% page and hidden it, and the
same split now keeps the settled window sensitive at its own ~15% scale
while the entry window gates at 7.53%.

_measuredNote: 8618e773 landed retail's 50-frame staged reveal and took this window
from 'we draw the whole page on frame 0' to 'we draw what retail draws'.
All ten regions moved and none was re-derived until 2026-07-28. What is
LEFT here is the honest remainder: the title logo and the top-right
emblem, the two layers retail forces opaque from frame 0, are still
22.17% and 12.96% wrong. Everything else is at or under 0.30%.
Seven of ten moved with 8618e773; bg-empty-left, bg-emblem-topright and
title-logo did not move at all. The worst remaining region is
lang-selector at 61.55% - retail is brighter there at 524 ms than the
ported fade model makes it, which 8618e773 recorded as explicitly NOT
closed rather than scaling a constant until it went away.

_samplesNote: Every settled retail run1 burst offset, not the five the hand
measurements used. The extra seven cost a few seconds and they are
the ones that would catch a phase regression that happens to look
fine at the five offsets a human picked.

unscored.reason: retail's own two runs disagree by 5.8-44.2% material at matched page-entry offsets, so no reconstruction improvement below that is measurable. Gating on it would be theatre.
